description: #5057 — `confirm_pairing`, the joiner half of pairing. Waived as 'pairing-window plumbing, not projected block state', which is the scope shape the ratchet's own doctrine rejects: it makes TWO durable writes, and they differ in whether anything can see them. The `pending_pairing` marker in `app_settings` is unobservable for the reason `cancel_pairing` is permanently blocked — no command on either stack reads that key. The other is `clear_unpaired_by_peer_all`, which drops the #4297 'this peer says we are not paired' flag from EVERY `peer_refs` row, and `list_peer_refs` projects that column. So the step below is the observation, exactly as it is for the three peer writers in `peer_ref_writes.json`. Only ONE `list_peer_refs` read follows the confirm, deliberately: the mock arms a pending peer reveal that materializes a TOFU-pinned row on the THIRD read (`PAIRING_PEER_REVEAL_READS`), standing in for the first authenticated connection that this harness has no transport for.
name: pairing_confirm

ops.comment: A joiner needs no local session and the passphrase is never compared here — it is hashed into the pending marker, and a wrong one is only discovered on the wire. So this succeeds for any input, and what it leaves behind is the flag clear below.
ops.name: confirm_a_typed_passphrase

queries.comment: The observation: `peer-flagged` has lost its unpaired stamp and every other column is untouched — the clear is scoped to one column, not to one peer, because neither pairing role knows yet which peer the passphrase resolves to.
queries.name: peers_after_confirm
